# poiema-ui — full context

Poiema design system (proprietary, Poiema use only): monochrome, tactile, editorial. Framework-agnostic CSS tokens + pm-* component classes, tiny optional JS behaviors, Tailwind v4 theme, and agent context (AGENTS.md, skills) so AI builds in the same voice.


---

# Poiema UI — instructions for coding agents

You are building UI with the **Poiema design system** (`poiema-ui`). It is **proprietary to Poiema** (see `LICENSE`): use it only in Poiema's own projects. Never publish it to npm or a public CDN, and never copy it into projects for anyone else. Follow these rules whenever you create or change anything users see: markup, styles, copy or motion. Details live in `docs/` next to this file (in an app: `node_modules/poiema-ui/docs/`).

## The essence
A **quiet gray gallery**. Huge, tight, **lowercase** type does the shouting. Soft 40px cards and pills. **No hue in the interface**: color lives only in tactile objects (clay, plaster, grass, iron, diamond). The voice is **sincere and communal** ("we", "our family"), and it gets to the point. Motion **rises and settles**; objects float.

## Decide first: site or app?
Everything else depends on this, and the wrong answer can't be fixed with polish.

- **A site** is read once: landing page, event page, institutional page, guide. Use the gallery register, which is the default and what most of this file describes.
- **An app** is used again and again: admin, portal, dashboard, internal tool, anything behind a login. Put `class="pm-app"` on `<html>` and **read `docs/app.md` before writing a screen.** Same room, working volume.

One product can be both: a public page in the gallery and `/admin` as an app.

**An app screen is never** a hero, a section head with a lead paragraph, or a stack of cards. It is `.pm-shell` (sidebar + tab bar) → `.pm-pagehead` (title + one line of state) → search and filter chips with counts → one `.pm-rows` card with a row per thing. On a list screen on a 390×844 phone, the first row starts within about 200px of the top. Creating or editing opens a `.pm-panel` over the list. A problem is fixed on its own row. Navigation never scrolls away.

## Setup (once per app)
- CSS: `import 'poiema-ui/css'` (or a self-hosted copy of `dist/poiema.min.css`). Tailwind v4: see `docs/frameworks.md`.
- Font: Inter Tight 400–900 (`poiema-ui/fonts.css`, `next/font` with `variable: '--pm-font-sans'`, or `@fontsource-variable/inter-tight`).
- Behaviors (optional): call `init()` from `poiema-ui` once on the client at the app root, or load `poiema-ui/auto`.

## Hard rules
1. **Use the `pm-*` classes and `--pm-*` tokens.** Don't invent colors, radii, shadows or fonts. If something is missing, compose it from tokens.
2. **Grayscale chrome only.** Backgrounds: `--pm-canvas` (page), `.pm-card`, `--pm-surface` (paper). Text: `--pm-ink`, `--pm-ink-2`, `--pm-label`, `--pm-muted`. Material colors (`--pm-clay`, `--pm-grass`…) are for objects, illustrations and data only, never buttons, links or backgrounds. Errors use `--pm-danger`, confirmations `--pm-success`.
3. **Never use pure white pages.** The page is `#e2e2e2`; cards are paper.
4. **Display headlines are lowercase and end with a period** (questions end with `?`): `<h2 class="pm-h1">your projects.</h2>`. Eyebrows, tags and alert titles are small, bold, UPPERCASE via CSS. In an app display means three roles: the page title, an empty state's title and a dialog's question. The rest is data and keeps its case, and a title that is a name stays a name (`Ana Souza`).
5. **One echo per display line:** wrap one phrase in `.pm-muted` (the gray middle beat): `plan. <span class="pm-muted">focus.</span> finish.`
6. **Soft geometry:** cards 40px (`.pm-card`), callouts 28px, alerts and tiles 24px, buttons/chips/inputs pill. Numbers in rings (`.pm-ring`), bullets are diamonds (`.pm-list`). `.pm-app` steps these down to 24/20/16/12 with fields at 12px, on its own: never hard-code a radius. In an app, rings are for steps only and counts go in badges.
7. **Key-message callouts only on request.** The reference page briefed leaders, so every section closed with a `.pm-callout` labeled "The message that must be clear" / "Mensagem que precisa ficar clara". Poiema products mostly speak to consumers: don't add that callout unless the user asks for it.
8. **Rhythm by inversion:** alternate `.pm-card` and `.pm-card[data-theme="dark"]`; use ink boxes (`.pm-inverse`) and the marquee band for punctuation, not color. Sites only: in an app the ink tab bar is the inversion, and black means chosen or primary.
9. **Motion:** `data-pm-reveal` on sections/cards, `.pm-float` + `data-pm-tilt` on objects only, curve `--pm-ease`. No bounce, no spin, no parallax. Reduced motion is handled; keep it that way. In an app, nothing moves on the way in: data is there the moment the screen is.
10. **Copy:** verb-first buttons (`Create project`), past-participle feedback (`Saved ✓`), calm alerts (`Attention` / `Important` + why), "we/our", no hype words, no emoji, at most one `!` (the closing line). Full guide: `docs/voice.md`.
11. **Accessibility:** keep semantic HTML, labels on fields, `aria-invalid` for errors, `aria-current`/`aria-selected` for active pills, alt text on objects (`alt=""` if decorative), visible focus (already styled).

## Cheat-sheet

```
page        body (canvas) > .pm-topbar + main > .pm-section > .pm-container
hero        .pm-hero(.pm-hero--pillars) > .pm-eyebrow + .pm-lockup|.pm-display + .pm-cluster(.pm-chip…) + .pm-lead + .pm-scroll-cue
title       .pm-section-head > .pm-ring + .pm-h1 + p
card        .pm-card | [data-theme=dark] | --outline | --compact      tile: .pm-tile
feature     .pm-card.pm-feature(--flip) > .pm-feature__media[data-pm-tilt] > img.pm-object.pm-float + .pm-feature__body
callout     .pm-callout > .pm-eyebrow + p (+ p.pm-callout__big)
alert       .pm-alert(--danger|--success) > strong.pm-alert__title + p
lists       .pm-list (◆) | --check (✓ must keep) | --open (○ your call) | --numbered
buttons     .pm-btn | --soft | --outline | --ghost | --danger | --sm | --lg | --icon | --block | --rich(__icon __text __arrow)
chips       .pm-chip | --solid | --outline     .pm-tag (outlined uppercase)
nav         .pm-pillnav(--sticky) > a|button (+ .pm-ring--sm), active = aria-current / aria-selected / aria-pressed
data        .pm-stat(__value __label) .pm-numeral .pm-ticket(__main __dates __month __side __row) .pm-table .pm-progress
forms       div.pm-field > label.pm-label[for] + (.pm-input|.pm-select|.pm-textarea)[id][aria-describedby] + (.pm-hint|.pm-error)[id] ; label.pm-choice > .pm-check|.pm-radio|.pm-switch
overlay     dialog.pm-dialog (+ data-pm-open="id", data-pm-close) ; toast('Saved ✓')
layout      .pm-container .pm-section .pm-band .pm-stack(--sm|--lg|--xl) .pm-cluster .pm-grid(--2|--3) .pm-split .pm-ruled
type        .pm-eyebrow .pm-display .pm-h1 .pm-h2 .pm-h3 .pm-h4 .pm-lead .pm-body .pm-small .pm-numeral .pm-prose
utility     .pm-muted .pm-ink-2 .pm-nums .pm-center .pm-measure .pm-lower .pm-sr-only .pm-inverse .pm-lift
themes      data-theme="light|dark|auto" on any element
motion [JS] data-pm-reveal(="fade"|"scale") data-pm-stagger data-pm-tilt data-pm-cycle data-pm-copy data-pm-countdown
```

Apps (`html.pm-app`):
```
screen      .pm-shell > .pm-sidebar + main.pm-shell__main > .pm-pagehead + content ; then .pm-tabbar + .pm-fab
sidebar     .pm-sidebar > .pm-sidebar__brand + .pm-sidebar__nav > .pm-sidebar__group > .pm-sidebar__title + a[aria-current] ; .pm-sidebar__user
tabs        nav.pm-tabbar > a[aria-current]  (2-4, Menu last)
head        .pm-pagehead(--pin) > .pm-pagehead__line > .pm-pagehead__title(h1.pm-h1 + .pm-pagehead__sub) + .pm-pagehead__actions
filter      .pm-toolbar > label.pm-search(input + .pm-search__clear[data-pm-clear]) ; .pm-pillnav--bleed > button[aria-pressed] + .pm-count, [data-tone=danger], .pm-flag
list        .pm-rows(--columns) > .pm-rows__head | .pm-rows__label | .pm-rows__section | .pm-rows__empty | .pm-row
row         .pm-row(--danger|--off|--add) > .pm-row__text(.pm-row__title + .pm-row__sub(--danger)) + one trailing item ; .pm-row__link stretches over the row
facts       .pm-badge(--solid|--danger|--outline|--dashed) .pm-count .pm-flag .pm-datetile(--sm) .pm-datestrip .pm-stats .pm-bars[tabindex=0](> span[style=--v][data-value][data-label]) + .pm-bars__axis ; progress.pm-progress as a row's last child
states      .pm-empty(__icon __title) .pm-notice(--draft|--danger) .pm-disclosure .pm-faded .pm-skeleton
overlays    dialog.pm-sheet (__title __sub __actions) quick choice ; dialog.pm-panel (__head __title __sub __body __foot) forms ; dialog.pm-dialog (__foot) confirm
actions     .pm-fab ; dialog.pm-fabmenu > .pm-menu + .pm-fab[data-pm-close] ; [popover].pm-menu[data-pm-menu trigger] > .pm-menu__item(--primary|--danger) > .pm-menu__icon + .pm-menu__label + .pm-menu__hint
inputs      .pm-segmented > label > input + span ; .pm-stepper > button + output + button
layout      .pm-workspace > main + .pm-workspace__rail > .pm-todo ; .pm-selectbar ; .pm-gate ; .pm-phone-only .pm-desk-only (900px) .pm-narrow-only .pm-wide-only (1280px)
feedback    toast('Removed ✓', { action: { label: 'Undo', onClick } })
```

Key tokens: `--pm-canvas --pm-surface --pm-surface-2 --pm-card --pm-ink --pm-ink-2 --pm-label --pm-muted --pm-line --pm-divider --pm-danger --pm-danger-soft --pm-success --pm-font --pm-text-h1 --pm-radius-xl --pm-gutter --pm-section --pm-ease --pm-shadow-float --pm-shadow-card --pm-shadow-pop`. Full list: `docs/tokens.md`.

## Before you finish a UI task, check
- [ ] No hex colors or hues outside tokens; no Tailwind default palette; no pure white page.
- [ ] Every display headline is lowercase and ends with `.`/`?`; one `.pm-muted` echo at most per line.
- [ ] No key-message `.pm-callout` unless the user asked for one.
- [ ] Radii come from tokens, never hard-coded; bullets are diamonds.
- [ ] Motion only via the catalogue in `docs/motion.md`.
- [ ] Copy follows `docs/voice.md` (verb-first buttons, ✓ feedback, no emoji).

Building a site? Also: radii read 40/28/24/pill and numbers sit in rings.

Building an app? Also, seen at 390px and 1440px:
- [ ] `pm-app` is on `<html>`; navigation is `.pm-sidebar` + `.pm-tabbar`, from one list.
- [ ] On a list screen the first row of data starts within about 200px of the top on a phone. No hero, no lead paragraph.
- [ ] Lists are one `.pm-rows` card, not a card per item. Names wrap, never cut.
- [ ] Filters answer as you type or tap; chips show counts; no submit button.
- [ ] One filled button per screen; when a list is empty, the empty state holds it. Destructive is the clay wash. Create and edit open a `.pm-panel`.
- [ ] A problem is written or flagged, and its fix is on its own row.
- [ ] Loading, empty and error are designed. 44px targets on touch, fields 16px on touch.

## Docs map
**`docs/app.md` building apps, portals, admins** · `docs/principles.md` tone & mood · `docs/voice.md` conversation style · `docs/color.md` · `docs/typography.md` · `docs/layout.md` · `docs/motion.md` · `docs/components.md` (every class with HTML) · `docs/imagery.md` · `docs/frameworks.md` (Next, Svelte, Vue, Astro, Tailwind, plain HTML) · `docs/tokens.md` (generated). Skills: `skills/poiema-design`, `skills/poiema-voice`, `skills/poiema-review`. Working examples: `demo/index.html` (site), `demo/app.html` (app).

---

## Working on this repository (not on an app)
- `src/tokens.json` is the single source for tokens. `src/css/*.css` holds components (each file declares its `@layer`). `src/js/poiema.js` holds behaviors (keep every export a top-level `export function`/`export const`; the auto build strips `export`).
- `npm run build` regenerates `dist/`, `docs/tokens.md`, the contrast table in `docs/color.md`, `skills/*/references/` and `llms-full.txt`. **Never edit generated files by hand.** Commit `dist/` (GitHub installs use it; there is no public CDN).
- `npm test` builds and runs `test/`. The build fails if a contrast pair in `src/tokens.json` drops below its threshold.
- New component: add CSS in the right file, document it in `docs/components.md` (HTML snippet), add it to the cheat-sheet above and to `demo/index.html` (`demo/app.html` for app components).
- The app register is token-first: `app` in `src/tokens.json` re-points existing tokens, and the build fails on a name that doesn't exist. Reach for a token before a `.pm-app` selector. Nothing in `src/css/app.css` may change a page without `.pm-app`: scope any rule on an existing component with `:is(.pm-app, .pm-shell)`.
- After visual changes, refresh the README images with `npm run screenshots` (needs Playwright: `npm i --no-save playwright`). `screenshots/` is not shipped in the package.
- Releases come only from the **Release** workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, run from GitHub Actions): it bumps `package.json` and the plugin manifest, points install snippets at the new `#semver:` range, rebuilds, writes `CHANGELOG.md`, tags `vX.Y.Z` and publishes a GitHub release listing the commits since the last tag. Never bump the version, edit `CHANGELOG.md` or tag by hand. Bump `patch` for docs, skills and fixes, `minor` for new components or tokens, `major` for renamed or removed classes and tokens or rules that make agents rewrite existing screens (while on `0.x`, breaking changes go out as `minor`).
- Zero runtime dependencies. Keep it that way.


---

# Principles — tone & mood

> **Poiema** (ποίημα): *workmanship, something made*. The system grew out of the direction page for Poiema Conf 26. Its central image is material being formed: **clay → plaster → grass → iron → diamond**. The interface is the quiet studio, and the objects carry the transformation.

## The mood in one line

**A quiet gray gallery, huge confident lowercase type, and a few tactile objects floating in soft light. It is sincere and communal, and it never shouts in color.**

| It feels | It never feels |
|---|---|
| quiet, weighty, calm | loud, busy, "growth-hacky" |
| tactile and physical (objects, shadows, paper) | flat, glossy, neon, gradient-heavy |
| editorial and poster-like (on a site); calm and direct (in an app) | template-like, a stock admin kit |
| sincere and pastoral ("we", "our family") | salesy, ironic, jokey |
| clear and decisive | vague, hedging |
| contemporary and reverent | churchy-clichéd, or cold-corporate |

## The eight principles

### 1. Gray is the room; objects carry the color
Interface chrome is strictly **grayscale**: canvas `#e2e2e2`, paper `#f7f7f7`, ink `#2b2b2b`. Hue appears only inside **material objects** such as 3D renders, photos and the gem, and in the rare semantic state (danger = clay, success = grass). Never paint buttons, links or backgrounds with a hue.

### 2. Type does the shouting
Hierarchy comes from **scale, weight and tight tracking** in one family (Inter Tight). Headlines are huge, heavy (800), tightly tracked (-0.05em), **lowercase, and end with a period**: `watch first.` Everything around them is small and calm: 12px tracked uppercase eyebrows, 17px body.

### 3. Soft geometry
Every container is soft: **40px cards, pill buttons and chips, circular rings**. The only sharp shape is the small rotated-square **diamond** bullet, which echoes the gem. No 4px or 8px "app" corners on large surfaces.

### 4. One point per section
Each section makes one point, and its headline and first line carry it. Write for skimmers. The reference page, a briefing for leaders, repeated that point in an ink callout labeled *"the message that must be clear"*; Poiema products mostly speak to consumers, so add that callout only when someone asks for it.

### 5. Rhythm by inversion
Light cards and dark cards alternate. Ink boxes punctuate paper. A dark marquee band breaks the page. Contrast, not color, creates emphasis and pacing.

### 6. Numbers are structure
Content is a numbered journey: `00 watch first.` → `01` … `07`. Numbers sit in **rings**, the same drawing as the "26" badge of the logo. Dates are typographic: `13 · 14 · 15 nov`, `18.10.2026`.

### 7. Motion settles
Things **rise 28px and settle** (900ms, `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`). Objects **float** on a slow 7s breath and tilt toward the pointer. Materials **cross-fade**. Nothing bounces, flashes or spins for fun, and everything respects reduced motion.

### 8. Freedom with clear boundaries
The voice separates **what must be kept** (✓ checks) from **what is up to you** (○ open circles). It explains the *why* behind every rule and trusts the reader.

## Do / don't

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use `--pm-canvas` gray as the page, paper cards on top | Use pure white `#fff` pages or colored backgrounds |
| One huge lowercase headline per section, ending in `.` | Title Case Headlines Or ALL CAPS HEADLINES |
| Make one phrase gray (`.pm-muted`) to create an echo: `from christ. <span class="pm-muted">in us.</span> to the world.` | Use color or underline for emphasis in display type |
| Put the main point in the headline and first line | Bury it mid-paragraph, or repeat it in a callout nobody asked for |
| Pills for actions, rings for numbers, diamonds for bullets | Square buttons, emoji bullets, icon-font clutter |
| Real objects with soft drop shadows, floating | Flat stock illustrations, glossy 3D blobs, gradients as decoration |
| Calm outlined alerts ("Attention", "Important") | Red/yellow alert banners and exclamation icons |
| Slow reveal on scroll and gentle float | Bouncy springs, parallax overload, auto-playing noise |

## Two registers: gallery and app
The system is not tied to its source, but it doesn't speak at one volume. Everything above describes the **gallery**: pages people read once. A store's front page or an event page belongs there.

Something people come back to and use is an **app**: an admin, a portal, a dashboard, an internal tool. It keeps the gray room, paper, ink, one typeface, lowercase page titles, the voice and no hue in the chrome. It turns the volume down: small titles, one card with a row per thing, navigation that stays put and no motion on content. A huge headline there only pushes the work below the fold. Start with `class="pm-app"` and follow `docs/app.md`.


---

# The app register

**Same room, working volume.** Poiema has two registers. The gallery is for things people read once. The app register is for things people come back to and use.

| It's a **site** (the gallery) when… | It's an **app** (`.pm-app`) when… |
|---|---|
| people read it once and leave | people return to get a job done |
| landing page, event page, institutional page, guide | admin, portal, dashboard, internal tool, signed-in area |
| the headline is the point | the data is the point |

Decide first. One product can hold both: a public page in the gallery and `/admin` as an app.

The register changes volume, never identity. It keeps the gray room, paper, ink, one typeface, lowercase titles, the voice and no hue in the chrome. `demo/app.html` is a working example (in an app: `node_modules/poiema-ui/demo/app.html`): read its markup when a snippet leaves you guessing.

| | Gallery | App |
|---|---|---|
| Page title | `.pm-h1` 40–88px | `.pm-h1` 26–34px, same class |
| Page opens with | hero, section head, lead paragraph | title, one line of state, then the data |
| Cards | 40px radius, 28–72px padding, paper gradient | 24px radius, 16–24px padding, flat paper |
| A list | a stack of cards | **one card with a row per thing** (`.pm-rows`) |
| Navigation | topbar that scrolls away | sidebar on a desk, floating tab bar on a phone |
| Main action | a big button in the page | header button on a desk, circle above the tab bar on a phone |
| Forms | a page of their own | a panel over the list they belong to |
| Fields | 52px pills | 44px on touch, 40px with a mouse, 12px radius |
| Motion | reveal on scroll, float, tilt | none on content, overlays only |
| Hover | lift | quiet tint |
| Numbers | rings, huge numerals | counts in badges; rings only for steps |

## Turn it on

```html
<html lang="pt-BR" class="pm-app" data-theme="light">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
```
`.pm-app` re-points the tokens, so `.pm-btn`, `.pm-card`, `.pm-h1`, `.pm-input`, `.pm-dialog` and the rest follow with no other change. Put it on `<html>` so dialogs, popovers and toasts inherit it. An app inside a larger site can put it on a layout wrapper instead; `.pm-shell` applies it on its own. `viewport-fit=cover` is what lets the tab bar clear the phone's home indicator.

Icons are not part of this package. Use [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) (`lucide-react`, or inline SVG), 2px stroke, `currentColor`. The components size them.

## The screen

Every signed-in screen is this. Copy it, then fill it in.

```html
<div class="pm-shell">
  <aside class="pm-sidebar">
    <a class="pm-sidebar__brand" href="/">poiema</a>
    <nav class="pm-sidebar__nav" aria-label="Main">
      <div class="pm-sidebar__group">
        <p class="pm-sidebar__title">Work</p>
        <a href="/people" aria-current="page"><svg>…</svg>People</a>
        <a href="/schedule"><svg>…</svg>Schedule <span class="pm-badge pm-badge--danger"><span class="pm-flag"></span>3<span class="pm-sr-only"> to fix</span></span></a>
      </div>
    </nav>
    <div class="pm-sidebar__user">
      <strong>Marina Duarte</strong> Administrator
      <div class="pm-cluster"><a href="/profile">My profile</a><button type="button">Sign out</button></div>
    </div>
  </aside>

  <main class="pm-shell__main">
    <header class="pm-pagehead">
      <div class="pm-pagehead__line">
        <div class="pm-pagehead__title">
          <h1 class="pm-h1">people.</h1>
          <p class="pm-pagehead__sub">167 people · 6 on vacation</p>
        </div>
        <div class="pm-pagehead__actions">           <!-- desk only -->
          <button class="pm-btn pm-btn--soft">Select several</button>
          <button class="pm-btn">Add person</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="pm-toolbar"><!-- .pm-search --></div>
      <div class="pm-pillnav pm-pillnav--bleed" role="group" aria-label="Filter"><!-- chips with counts --></div>
    </header>

    <div class="pm-rows pm-rows--columns"><!-- .pm-row, one per person --></div>
  </main>
</div>

<nav class="pm-tabbar" aria-label="Main">      <!-- phone only -->
  <a href="/people" aria-current="page"><svg>…</svg>People</a>
  <a href="/schedule"><svg>…</svg>Schedule</a>
  <a href="/menu"><svg>…</svg>Menu</a>
</nav>
<button class="pm-fab" data-pm-open="actions" aria-label="Actions for this screen"><svg>…</svg></button>   <!-- phone only -->
```

The sidebar and tab bar show or hide themselves at 900px, and so do `.pm-pagehead__actions` and `.pm-fab`. iPads in portrait get the tab bar: they are wide, but they are touched.

**The test:** on a list screen, on a 390×844 phone, the first row of data starts within about 200px of the top. If it doesn't, something above it is decoration. A screen that first has to say something (a draft to approve, a set of days to jump between) may spend more, as long as it's doing a job.

## The rules

These come from the church's rota app, which leaders use on their phones and the admin at a desk. Each one exists because something went wrong without it.

1. **Understood in two seconds.** Title, then one line that says what is happening: `167 people · 6 on vacation`. Not a sentence about what the screen is for.
2. **Navigation stays put.** Two to four tabs on a phone, Menu always last, and everything else inside Menu. On a desk, a sidebar in named groups. Build both from one list, so they can't drift apart.
3. **Screen actions have one home.** On a desk they are header buttons, and rarely used ones wait in a `⋯` menu. On a phone they live in the circle above the tab bar, in the same spot on every screen. Screens with none have no circle. One action: the circle is that action (`+`). Two or more: `⋯` opens them, with the main one last, closest to the thumb.
4. **One filled button per screen,** for what completes the job. Everything else is `--soft`, `--outline` or `--ghost`. Destructive buttons are a pale clay wash, never filled. When a list is empty, the empty state holds the action and the header stops offering it.
5. **A list is one card with a row per thing.** Not a card per thing. Rows are 44px or taller, with a title, an optional line under it, and a chevron or one trailing item.
6. **Names are never cut.** They wrap. A truncated name is a different person. Full names, no initials, no avatars unless there are real photos.
7. **Fix it where you see it.** A problem carries its own button: an open seat says `Choose`, right there. Never send someone to a menu or another screen to fix what they are looking at.
8. **Filtering answers immediately.** No submit button, no apply button. Chips show their count before you tap (`On vacation 6`), so a tap is never a guess. Counts follow the search. Hide a chip that has nothing at all, unless it's the active one; while someone is typing, keep the row still and let a 0 be the answer. Three big selects are a filter that nobody uses; a chip row and one search box are not. A second kind of filter goes behind one button that opens a sheet, and fills with ink (`aria-pressed="true"`) while it's on. If the whole list is small enough to send (hundreds of rows), filter in the browser and keep the URL in step; otherwise debounce a server query.
9. **The overlay fits the job.** See the table below. Creating or editing something keeps you on the list you came from.
10. **Clay means a problem, and is never alone.** Nothing else in the chrome has a hue. A problem is always written (`2 open seats`) or marked with `.pm-flag`, the one sharp shape in the system, so it reads without its color.
11. **No surprises on big actions.** Say exactly what will change before it happens. What can be reversed gets a toast with Undo, not a confirmation. What can't gets a dialog, with focus on Cancel.
12. **Wide screens show more, not longer.** `.pm-rows--columns` flows rows into two columns, then three. A rail (`.pm-workspace`) holds the to-do list. A row never stretches across 1400px. Only a short notice or a form stays narrow (`.pm-measure`).
13. **Nothing animates on the way in.** Data is there the moment the screen is. `data-pm-reveal` and `data-pm-stagger` do nothing inside `.pm-app`, on purpose. Only overlays move, and quickly.
14. **Every state is designed.** Loading looks like the screen it stands in for. Empty says what will be here and offers the button that starts it. Errors say what happened and offer to try again.
15. **Thumbs and mice both.** 44px targets on touch, compact with a mouse. Fields stay at 16px or more on touch, or iOS zooms the page.

## Which overlay

| Doing | Use | Phone | Desk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tapped a name; a short choice | `.pm-sheet` | rises from the bottom | centered, 420px |
| Create or edit; pick from a long list | `.pm-panel` | full screen, back arrow | panel on the right, list still visible. Cancel means nothing happened: reset the form on the dialog's `close` event |
| Confirm something irreversible | `.pm-dialog` | centered | centered |
| Actions for this screen | `.pm-fab` + `dialog.pm-fabmenu` | blurs the screen | header buttons |
| A few more actions | `.pm-menu[popover]` + `data-pm-menu` | not needed, use the circle | under the `⋯` button |

A form earns its own page only when it is the whole job, like settings. Otherwise, use a panel. A field with a button beside it is `.pm-toolbar` > `.pm-input` + `.pm-btn`; `.pm-input-group` is for the gallery's pill fields.

## Which screen

| Screen | Build it from |
|---|---|
| A list of things | `.pm-pagehead` + `.pm-search` + `.pm-pillnav` chips + `.pm-rows.pm-rows--columns` |
| One thing | `.pm-pagehead` with a back button; its name is the title. `.pm-workspace` if it has a side column. Under 1280px the rail falls below everything, so if its content matters sooner, mark the rail `.pm-wide-only` and offer the same thing as a `.pm-narrow-only` row that opens a sheet |
| A month or a set of days | `.pm-datestrip`, one `.pm-rows` per day in a `.pm-grid`, `.pm-workspace__rail` with `.pm-todo` |
| Something awaiting approval | `.pm-notice.pm-notice--draft` above the data, `.pm-badge--dashed` beside the title |
| Numbers | `.pm-stats`, `.pm-bars` + `.pm-bars__axis` (every bar reads out its value and date, on hover and on touch), `.pm-row` with a `<progress class="pm-progress">` as its last child |
| Settings | `.pm-stack.pm-measure` of `.pm-card` and `.pm-rows` with switches and steppers |
| Everything that isn't a tab | A Menu screen: `.pm-rows` with an icon first and a line under each title. Language and sign out live here on a phone, and in `.pm-sidebar__user` on a desk, where Menu's other rows are already in the sidebar |
| Selecting many | Rows become `label.pm-row` with `.pm-check`; `.pm-selectbar` holds what to do |
| Sign in, not found, error | `.pm-gate` with one card, no navigation |
| Tables | `.pm-table` in a `.pm-card`, from 900px up. Under 900px, list the same data as rows |

## Copy in an app

The voice doesn't change. Where it lands does. **Three things are display, lowercase with a period or question mark:** the page title (`people.`), an empty state's title (`nothing here yet.`) and a dialog's question (`delete this link?`).

**Everything else is data, which keeps its case and takes no period,** whatever class it uses: a section of a screen (`Campaigns`), card headers (`Sunday, Nov 8`), rows, badges, panel titles (`Create link`).
- **A title that is a name stays a name:** `Easter service signup`, `Ana Souza`. Never `ana souza.`
- **No lead paragraph.** The sub-line states facts: `Kids · 4 Sundays · 3 open seats`.
- Rings are for steps. Counts go in a `.pm-badge` or `.pm-count`.

## Building it in React

Keep the classes; only the wiring is yours. Three things pay for themselves:

- **One nav list** (`{ key, href, label, icon, group }`) that renders both the sidebar and the tab bar, with the tabs chosen per role.
- **One action list per screen** (`{ id, label, hint, icon, primary, more, danger, onSelect }`), mapped to header buttons and to `.pm-menu__item`. The screen declares its actions once.
- **`init()` once at the root.** It wires `<dialog>`s, popover menus and `data-pm-clear` as they mount, however the route changes.

Native `<dialog>` gives you focus trapping, Esc and the top layer with no library, and `popover` gives a small menu Esc, a tap away and the top layer. Call `el.showModal()`, or use `data-pm-open`.

**Hydration.** `init()` adds nothing to the page: no children, no attributes. So a server-rendered screen still matches when React hydrates it, and what a behavior reads has to be in your markup, like the chart's `tabindex`. Rely on `data-pm-reveal` only on sites: it does write an attribute.

**Hidden routes.** With Next's `cacheComponents` (and anything using React's `<Activity>`) a route you left stays mounted under `display: none`. A modal left open there keeps the next page inert and locked against scrolling, so close it when the route hides, and give popovers ids that are unique per screen (`useId`):
```tsx
function AppDialog(props: ComponentProps<'dialog'>) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);
  useLayoutEffect(() => { const el = ref.current; return () => el?.close(); }, []);
  return <dialog ref={ref} {...props} />;
}
```
A `[data-pm-open]` button finds the dialog on the visible screen by itself. In the DOM the old route's headings still exist, so scope test selectors with `:visible`.

To put a `<form>` around a panel's head, body and foot, give the form `style="display:contents"` so the panel's layout still applies. A menu closes when an item is chosen, so an item that copies should confirm with `toast('Copied ✓')`: `data-pm-copy`'s label swap would disappear with the menu.

## What not to do

These are what the gallery's habits look like when they land in a tool:

- An 88px title and a lead paragraph above the data. The first row starts 700px down.
- A card per item, each with a shadow and a hover lift: five items per screen.
- `data-pm-stagger` on a list. The rows are invisible until JavaScript runs.
- Navigation that scrolls away with the page, and sign out at the bottom of a long list.
- A search box with a Search button, plus two labeled selects, before any result.
- A new page for every form, losing the list behind it.
- `.pm-h2` in a dialog at 58px. With `.pm-app` on, it is a sensible size. Without it, it isn't.

## Known limits

- **The circle floats over content.** On a phone it can sit on top of a trailing button at rest. Scrolling moves the row out from under it, and the main column's bottom padding lets the last row clear it.
- **Toasts live under an open overlay.** While a sheet, panel or dialog is open the rest of the page is inert, so close it first, then call `toast()`. An Undo offered behind a modal can't be pressed.
- **Icons are yours.** The package ships none. `aria-hidden` on every decorative one, and a visible label on anything but the universal ones: close, back, search, menu, more, add.


---

# Voice — conversation style

The voice is a **pastor-editor**: warm, communal, sure of itself and brief. It speaks as **"we"** to **"our family"**, explains the *why*, draws clear boundaries and leaves room for freedom. Examples come in Portuguese (the brand's native language) and English. Apply the same rules in either.

## The ten patterns

### 1. Lowercase display headlines that end with a period
Headlines are statements, so they get a period. Questions keep their `?`.

| pt-BR | en |
|---|---|
| `assista primeiro.` | `watch first.` |
| `orientações gerais às lideranças.` | `general guidance for leaders.` |
| `por que não vamos divulgar o lineup?` | `why we won't announce the lineup?` |
| `suas tarefas de hoje.` | `your tasks for today.` |

Body text uses normal sentence case. Proper nouns stay capitalized in body copy and are lowercased only in display headlines (`o que é a poiema conference?`).

### 2. Triads with periods
Three short beats, each closed by a period. In display type the **middle beat goes gray** (`.pm-muted`), which creates the "echo."
- `de cristo. em nós. para o mundo.` / `from christ. in us. to the world.`
- In running text, use a comma triad: `com unidade, clareza e alinhamento` / `with unity, clarity and alignment`.
- App example: `plan. focus. finish.`

### 3. Reframe: "not X — Y"
Say what something is *not* before saying what it is. This is the signature rhetorical move.
- `Não é apenas uma programação de três dias. É um tempo de…` / `It isn't just a three-day schedule. It's a time of…`
- `Este material não é um roteiro de fala.` / `This isn't a script.`
- `Mais do que um evento, …` / `More than an event, …`
- `não apenas …, mas também …` / `not only …, but also …`

### 4. The message that must be clear (only on request)
The reference page briefed leaders, so each section closed with one or two sentences in a `.pm-callout` labeled **"Mensagem que precisa ficar clara"** / **"The message that must be clear"**. Poiema products mostly speak to consumers, so don't add it by default. When someone asks for it, keep it to one or two sentences that carry the point on their own.

### 5. Communal "we", warm and direct
Use `nós / nossa família / queremos / cremos` and `we / our family / we want / we believe`. Address the reader as a partner and never as a customer. No hype words ("incrível", "revolutionary", "🚀").

### 6. Freedom with boundaries
Split guidance explicitly into what must be kept (`.pm-list--check`) and what is up to the reader (`.pm-list--open`), then add one calm `.pm-alert` that guards the meaning:
> **Important.** Freedom in how you say it should not change what it means.

### 7. Calm alerts that explain
Alerts are titled with one uppercase word, **Atenção / Attention** or **Importante / Important**. They say what *not* to do and *why*, without blame and without exclamation marks.

### 8. Short verb-first actions, past-tense feedback
- Buttons: verb + object. `Baixar motions`, `Copiar informações`, `Assistir 2:43` / `Download files`, `Copy details`, `Watch 2:43`.
- Feedback: past participle + ✓. `Copiado ✓` / `Copied ✓`, `Salvo ✓` / `Saved ✓`.
- Failure: plain and blameless. `Não foi possível copiar` / `Couldn't copy`.
- Rich CTA subtitle: one line of *what you get*. `Pasta com os arquivos para cada telão` / `Folder with files for every screen`.

### 9. Typographic data
- Separate metadata with a middle dot and spaces: `Material interno · Poiemas`, `Tangaroa Hall · Taubaté`.
- Dates: `13 · 14 · 15 nov`, `18.10.2026`, `novembro · 2026`.
- Numbers are heroes: `19` (years), `26 dias` (countdown). Let one number be huge.
- Index steps with two digits in rings: `00`, `01` … `07`. `00` means "before everything".

### 10. Close with a couplet
End a page with an antithesis or anaphora pair, the one line people repeat:
- `Não venha por um nome. Venha por Jesus!` / `Don't come for a name. Come for Jesus!`
- App example: `Not more features. Fewer, better ones.`
The closing line is the only place an exclamation mark may appear.

## Microcopy kit (app contexts)

| Situation | pt-BR | en |
|---|---|---|
| Page title | `seus projetos.` | `your projects.` |
| Empty state title | `nada por aqui ainda.` | `nothing here yet.` |
| Empty state body | `Quando você criar o primeiro projeto, ele aparece aqui.` | `When you create your first project, it shows up here.` |
| Primary action | `Criar projeto` | `Create project` |
| Destructive confirm | `excluir projeto?` + `Isso não pode ser desfeito.` | `delete project?` + `This can't be undone.` |
| Success toast | `Projeto criado ✓` | `Project created ✓` |
| Error (form) | `Informe um e-mail válido.` | `Enter a valid email.` |
| Error (system) | `Algo não funcionou. Tente de novo em instantes.` | `Something didn't work. Try again in a moment.` |
| Loading | `Carregando…` | `Loading…` |
| Section eyebrow | `Passo 02 · Detalhes` | `Step 02 · Details` |
| Key-message callout label (on request) | `Mensagem que precisa ficar clara` | `The one thing to remember` |
| Onboarding step | `00 · comece por aqui.` | `00 · start here.` |

### In an app
The voice stays; it just talks less. No lead paragraphs, triads or couplets on a working screen.

| Situation | pt-BR | en |
|---|---|---|
| Page title | `pessoas.` | `people.` |
| Line under it: facts, not a pitch | `167 pessoas · 6 de férias` | `167 people · 6 on vacation` |
| A title that is a name: data, keeps its case, no period | `Ana Souza` | `Ana Souza` |
| Card header | `Domingo, 8 nov` | `Sunday, Nov 8` |
| Count in a badge | `3 pessoas` | `3 people` |
| A problem names the thing | `2 vagas` | `2 open seats` |
| The fix on the row | `Escolher` | `Choose` |
| Reversible action: do it, then offer | `Removido ✓` + `Desfazer` | `Removed ✓` + `Undo` |
| Irreversible: say what changes | `excluir este link?` + `Os QR codes impressos param de funcionar.` | `delete this link?` + `Printed QR codes stop working.` |
| No results | `Ninguém com esse nome.` | `Nobody with that name.` |

## Punctuation & casing rules
- Display headlines: lowercase, period at the end (or `?`). In an app that means the page title, empty-state titles and dialog questions; everything else on the screen is data and keeps its case.
- Eyebrows, tags and alert titles: UPPERCASE in CSS (`text-transform`), so write them in sentence case in the source.
- Buttons: Sentence case, no period.
- Body: sentence case, periods, `—` for asides, `…` for ellipsis.
- One `<strong>` per paragraph at most. It marks the phrase that must not be missed.
- No emoji. The only symbols in copy are `·`, `✓`, `○`, `↗` and `—`. Chrome draws its own: `›` on a row, `+` on an add row, and icons for close and back.

## Self-check before shipping copy
1. Does every display headline end with `.` or `?` and stay lowercase?
2. Does each section's headline and first line carry its one point? (No key-message callout unless asked.)
3. Did you use "we/our" instead of "the company/users"?
4. Is any rhetorical "not X — Y" or triad doing real work, or is it decoration? Use them where they mean something, at most once or twice per page.
5. Are buttons verb-first, and does feedback use a past participle + ✓?
6. Zero hype words, zero emoji, at most one exclamation mark (the closing line).

# Color

**The interface is grayscale. Color lives in objects.** The grays are the exact values of the reference page. The five **materials** were sampled from its 3D gem renders: barro, gesso, grama, ferro, diamante.

## Neutrals — the room

| Role | Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page | `--pm-canvas` | `#e2e2e2` cool mid-gray | `#161616` |
| Paper (chips, inputs, bands) | `--pm-surface` | `#f7f7f7` | `#262626` |
| Panel / card base | `--pm-surface-2` | `#ececec` | `#1f1f1f` |
| Card fill | `--pm-card` | `linear-gradient(160deg, #fafafa, #ececec)` | `#1f1f1f` |
| Text, icons, solid buttons | `--pm-ink` | `#2b2b2b` | `#f7f7f7` |
| Body copy | `--pm-ink-2` | `#555555` | `#b9b9b9` |
| Small labels | `--pm-label` | `#646464` | `#9a9a9a` |
| Echo gray (large text only) | `--pm-muted` | `#7d7d7d` | `#8d8d8d` |
| Hairlines | `--pm-line` | `rgba(43,43,43,.14)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.12)` |
| Between rows | `--pm-divider` | `rgba(43,43,43,.08)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.07)` |

Pure white `#fff` appears only as the 1px top highlight on cards (`--pm-card-edge`). Pages are never white.

## Materials — the objects

| Material | pt-BR | Token | Light | Base | Deep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clay | barro | `--pm-clay` | `#d47b4d` | `#b8562a` | `#903b14` |
| Plaster | gesso | `--pm-plaster` | `#edebe9` | `#cfcbc6` | `#a9a49d` |
| Grass | grama | `--pm-grass` | `#8aa83a` | `#4b650a` | `#2f4305` |
| Iron | ferro | `--pm-iron` | `#777164` | `#534d40` | `#2b261c` |
| Diamond | diamante | `--pm-diamond` | `#eef1f2` | `#c3c8ca` | `#8f989c` |

The order matters. It tells a story of **formation** (clay → diamond), so when you show all five, keep that sequence.

**Use materials for:** the gem and other illustrations, object renders, data-viz series, avatars and placeholders, a category dot.
**Never use materials for:** buttons, links, backgrounds, focus rings or borders of interactive UI.

### Semantic states
- `--pm-danger` (clay): errors and destructive actions. It's a warm earth tone, never alarm red. Pair it with text such as "Couldn't save", never color alone.
- `--pm-danger-soft` (a pale clay wash): behind danger text, on problem badges, destructive buttons in apps and problem notices.
- `--pm-success` (grass): confirmations.
- No "warning" or "info" hue. Use a neutral `.pm-alert` with an uppercase title.

### In an app
Cards are flat `--pm-surface`, because a gradient drifts into the canvas along a long list. **Black is emphasis: what's chosen, what's primary, a date, a fact worth a second look. Clay means a problem, and nothing else.** No green "active", no colored status chips: a state is a word, a check, or a dashed outline for "not final yet". A problem is always written or marked with `.pm-flag`, the clay diamond, so it survives without its color.

## Themes & inversion

- `data-theme="light" | "dark" | "auto"` on **any** element re-maps every semantic token for that subtree and paints it with `--pm-canvas`. Use it on `<html>` for the whole app, or on a single card for the dark-card rhythm. (`.pm-card` keeps its own card fill, `#1f1f1f` in dark.)
- `.pm-inverse` (built into `.pm-callout`, `.pm-marquee` and `.pm-ticket__main`) flips the foreground tokens and fills with ink: a **dark box on light pages and a paper box on dark cards**, automatically.
- Solid buttons use `--pm-ink` / `--pm-on-ink`, so they flip with the theme on their own.

## Accessibility

The build checks these pairs in both themes and fails if one regresses. `muted` is reserved for large display text, which needs 3:1. For small gray text, use `label` or `ink-2`. Small labels (`--pm-label`) are a little darker than the reference page's `#8a8a8a` so 12px uppercase text passes AA. Design tweak: the echo gray moved from `#8a8a8a` to `#7d7d7d` to pass 3:1 on the canvas.

<!-- contrast:start -->
| Foreground | Background | Light | Dark | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ink` | `canvas` | 10.93 | 16.89 | 4.5 (AA) |
| `ink` | `surface` | 13.22 | 14.13 | 4.5 (AA) |
| `ink` | `surface-2` | 11.99 | 15.39 | 4.5 (AA) |
| `ink-2` | `canvas` | 5.75 | 9.22 | 4.5 (AA) |
| `ink-2` | `surface` | 6.96 | 7.71 | 4.5 (AA) |
| `ink-2` | `surface-2` | 6.31 | 8.40 | 4.5 (AA) |

| `label` | `surface` | 5.52 | 5.38 | 4.5 (AA) |
| `label` | `surface-2` | 5.01 | 5.86 | 4.5 (AA) |

| `success` | `canvas` | 6.05 | 6.67 | 4.5 (AA) |
